A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and are readable, including their complete appendices. The proof overview and renumbered appendices can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical bounds, proofs, algorithms, and analytic examples, but no original experimental or numerical simulation outcomes.

after.justification: Figure 2 reports original numerical time-complexity calculations for three synthetic computation-power scenarios in homogeneous and heterogeneous settings. These are numerical illustrations, not measured optimizer runtimes.

M1.justification: The universal computation model, Rennala SGD, Malenia SGD, and their accelerated convex variants retain the same procedures. Added explanations and examples do not modify the algorithms.

E1.justification: Figure 2 adds numerical evaluation of synthetic irregular, periodic noisy, and outage power trajectories in both homogeneous and heterogeneous settings. v1 discusses related computation scenarios analytically but does not report these numerical evaluations.

E2.justification: No evaluated comparator is added or removed. Comparisons involving Minibatch SGD, Asynchronous SGD, and Picky SGD remain theoretical; the new figures do not benchmark competing algorithms.

E3.justification: Figure 2 introduces numerical evaluation of the implicit time-complexity sequences with L∆/ε = 10 and σ²/ε = 100 under the illustrated worker dynamics. This is an added numerical protocol, not a revision of an existing experiment.

E4.justification: Figure 2 adds small numerical case studies illustrating how implicit complexities can be calculated for irregular, noisy periodic, and outage dynamics when closed-form expressions are difficult. The existing analytic examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Probability and concentration arguments in the proofs are theoretical rather than experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figure 2 newly reports homogeneous/heterogeneous complexity pairs of 6.57/13.02 seconds for irregular powers, 2.34/2.53 for periodic noisy powers, and 77.04/84.62 for outages. These are added illustrative calculations, not same-setting performance improvements over v1.

T1.justification: v2 adds Example 6.6 and its Appendix I.2 derivation for heterogeneous powers of the form vi(t) = vi g(t). The main lower and upper bounds, their proofs, auxiliary lemmas, and convex results remain substantively unchanged. The new displayed bound has an iteration-factor inconsistency with its derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the claims of a universal computation model, tight homogeneous and heterogeneous time bounds, and optimality of Rennala and Malenia SGD. The added examples do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 newly explains why the earlier geometric waiting-time analysis cannot directly handle varying computation powers and motivates indicator concentration. The conclusion also explicitly identifies correlated computation dynamics and gradient randomness as an open problem.

D1.justification: Figure 2 supplies parameter ratios for its new numerical calculations, providing limited reproducibility information. It does not supply exact trajectory-generation rules, numerical tolerances, or code/data access; existing algorithm details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work membership is unchanged, but Appendix A.1 adds a substantive comparison with Tyurin and Richtárik (2023), distinguishing their waiting-time concentration argument from this work's indicator-based reasoning.

P1.justification: The proof overview moves from Section 7 to Appendix A. v2 also adds reading guidance in Section 4, an informal statement of Theorem 6.2, and limited explanatory prose. Most text and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 1 for constant worker powers and the three-panel Figure 2 for varying powers, with explanatory captions. Conference headers and page layout change, while the existing algorithm displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The new figures and expanded explanations improve accessibility. However, Example 6.6 extends the iteration-factor omission already present in v1's Example 6.5: Appendix I.2 derives t_k = G⁻¹(kδ), but Equation 21 omits the corresponding iteration-count factor while bounding its constant independently. With the core results unchanged, the explanatory gains and this inconsistency in the added result do not establish a reliable net quality improvement.
